title: After the merge: read it blind, ask the builder, tidy what it left
description:
## As asked

Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** This week's good results came from what happened after a merge. Two separate readers judged the change from its code alone, without the ticket. The builder was asked what it had left behind. The copies they named at the edges became a small follow-on straight away. On the four tickets where we did this, the area ended better each time. Today a person does every one of those steps by hand. The leftovers that aren't fixed go into a notebook on a research branch, which has to be copied to main by hand (LIN-4316).

**What we want.** Harbour carries this. When a ticket's change merges, Harbour asks two fresh readers to judge it from the code alone, and asks the builder what was hard and what it left behind. Where they name something left at the edges, Harbour files a small follow-on. That follow-on goes through the look-first step like any ticket, because a reader's claim is a claim, not a fact. Not every merge needs a follow-on. A follow-on that both readers judge better gets none of its own, and an area with nothing waiting is fine.

What isn't fixed goes into notes kept with the code on main, by area: what's been learned about making changes there, and what's waiting. That's how the next ticket in an area pulls it in, and it answers LIN-4316: the loop's notebook stops living off main. This ticket owns those notes. The look-first and Periodical changes in this round will read and feed them.

One question is open for you to judge. The follow-on can be its own ticket, or the tidy can happen inside the same run, before close-out. Three builders suggested the second, and every extra ticket pays the fixed costs again. Either way, each of these steps shows its cost on the ticket like any other step. Today the builder's answers are sent into its finished session, and their cost doesn't show up anywhere we can see.

**Source material, a starting point rather than a spec.** The readers' prompt we used is frozen on main at `docs/papers/harbour/cleaner-than-it-started-evidence/2026-11-06/prompts/blind-read-prompt.md`. We asked builders why the work was difficult and where the change bound, what they would have done first, what they would tidy now, what the ticket would have been if the area were how they'd want it, what the ticket or plan got wrong, and what their change left behind in the wider codebase.

**Appetite:** err larger.

**Done looks like:** a ticket merges and, without anyone dispatching anything, the two readings and the builder's answers appear. Any follow-on is filed and looked at first, and the area's notes say what's waiting.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Implementation Plan

**Implemented and closed (8 Nov 2026).** The plan was implemented as approved: John's in-run version, not the post-merge research rig. The two cuts below were the deviations from what was asked. Both were agreed by ruling (`lin4347-cuts`, "Accept both cuts").

**What landed.** Area notes live in `docs/areas/` in both repositories, with Lessons and Waiting sections, and LIN-4316 is closed. At `[done]`, the builder gets a separately costed leftover step that asks what its change left behind, and the parent's wake is held until that step ends. Review reads the leftovers at the edges. Close-out writes the notes and fixes on the PR branch before the merge, and files only follow-ons outside the area.

* LinearViewer: [#2357](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2357>), [#2358](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2358>), [#2359](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2359>), [#2360](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2360>) (LIN-4375), and [#2361](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2361>) (LIN-4376, the tidy-after). Deployed at `110e35e0`.
* simple-dispatcher: [#329](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/329>) and [#330](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/330>). The runner is at `cb79e00`.

**Cut by ruling, not delivered.** (1) Automatic look-first on filed follow-ons belongs to LIN-4370. (2) Follow-ons get no special stop rule: their leftovers inside their own area go to the notes, as for any ticket.

**Post-deploy, recorded for the operator.**

* The first close-out that receives a review-routed note must commit it before the merge. This has not been observed yet; see the close-out comment and PR #2359.
* The [harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>) server-log monitor for `[leftover] release-skipped` / `release failed`. The accepted claim-then-crash strand stays in the `runs-and-dispatch` Waiting notes.

Landed in three pieces: needs multiple sessions.

plan-review due: yes. This plan needs more than one session, changes the dispatch contract (a parent's wake can now be held and released), and loosens a guard.

The full plan, its revisions and the research are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

**Before you start (John, 7 Nov): build the everyday version, not our research rig.**

The aim is that anyone can run this loop simply. While building it, we ran extra checks to measure whether it worked, and the product doesn't need all of them:

- **Two blind readers per merge** were for measurement. In normal running, one read of what the change left behind is enough to find the edges. Review already reads every change, so consider whether it's the natural place to ask.
- **Most of the builder's after-questions** were research: difficulty, what it would have done first, the ideal ticket, whether the larger scope paid. The one that drives the tidy is "what did your change leave behind?"
- **The tidy as its own ticket** was so we could measure it. In normal running, tidying inside the same run, before close-out, is probably cheaper. Three builders said so, and every extra ticket pays the fixed costs again. Choose with that in mind.

Our research reads will stay as hand-run dispatches outside Harbour, so there's no need to build them in.

What matters most in the product is good notes: each area's notes say what's been learned about making changes there, and what's waiting, so the next ticket can pull it in.

**First entries for the area notes (7 Nov).** When the notes exist, these belong in them, for the next ticket in this area to pull. The area read of LIN-4345 and its tidy-after (`fdd57fe9..d65d8af0`) was better in both blind passes, so under the stop rule these get no further tidy-after.

- `isHermeticTestToken` is a third way of spelling the test-token check, beside `routes/workspace-api-steps.js` `isTestToken` and the inline checks in `routes/proxy-compute.js` and task-chat. It's a new owner that nothing has moved to yet.
- `dispatch-factory.js` tests `provider.name === 'linear'` because of a test-only transport.
- `effort-readout.js` still outputs the deleted name `GATE_DUE_MARKER`, which is pinned by goldens.
- `lib/recap-cache.js`: `parentAsked` sits between `extractHashableContext`'s doc comment and the function.
- `as-asked.js` repeats its "When it could go" paragraph three times.

**More entries for the area notes (8 Nov).** The area read of PR #2351 + LIN-4367 (`11dc1d7b..9c2a378a`) was better in both passes, so under the stop rule these go to the notes, not to a tidy-after.

- `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md` lists the eight deciding stages by name: a second copy of `DECIDE`'s membership that no test watches.
- Who may agree to a reduced ask is stated under two names: "cut" in `CUT`, and "narrowing" in the plan-review and review verdict text (`prompt-template-defs.js`, `completion-signals.js`). No test links them.
- The prompt-size ceiling history moved into `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md`, a file meant as an append-only follow-on-ratio log, between its Columns and Rows sections.
- `CUT` writes the closing contract's token order (`DECISION:` before `BLOCKED:`) into a scope line, beside `ASK`, which asks for a different shape.

## Survey open-0: LIN-4347 @ eeda7e448

**Why it's hard.** Harbour has no merge event. A merge is noticed only as a side effect: `createPipelineMergeRecorder` (`lib/close-out-merges.js`) runs fire-and-forget on a Done write, and the task-page PR check does the same. A merge made on GitHub that nobody follows up is never recorded. The close-out worker that merges is a leaf with no `dispatch` grant, so it can't queue readers. "Without anyone dispatching" needs a server-originated producer. The only model is `lib/ci-wake-sweep.js`: a scheduler tick, an owner gate, caps, and a once-per-result guard. Dispatching from inside the recorder's catch-all `try` would hide failures.

**Blind and costed pull against each other.** Any dispatch tied to an issue gets the brief hint (`lib/proxy-preamble.js:262`) and a token that can read the ticket. The original blind reads stayed blind by posting to another ticket (LIN-4150). Cost is read per issue and lineage anchor (`lib/cost-read.js`). Blind to the ticket yet costed on it means a new dispatch shape: anchored to the ticket, with no brief hint and no issue read. That's plumbing, not a prompt.

**Asking the builder.** Plan, implementation and fix rounds are separate sessions, and a lane worker (LIN-2242) lands several tickets in one lineage. `enqueueFollowUp` resumes the lineage tail and refuses a stopped run (409, LIN-4080), which is likely the state after close-out. That may explain why the cost of today's question doesn't show.

**Notes on main.** Every write means a PR, an Approve and a merge, and notes per area will conflict when two tickets in one area land close together. The only area key is `scripts/code-shape/areas.json`. The server never reads it, it covers LinearViewer only, and it has an `Other features` catch-all. simple-dispatcher has none, and the blind reads spanned both repos. Main already holds `docs/plans/survey/` (log, `place-ledger.md`, `broad-options.md`). The new notes must replace those, or there will be a third home.

**Overlap.** `retrospective-audit` already runs after a merge (router rule 2). Unless one absorbs the other, the blind read would be a second post-merge reader. `survey-task` and `survey-place` are "hand-triggered only, never routed", so "goes through look-first like any ticket" isn't true for any ticket yet. It depends on the sibling look-first change.

**What I'd do first.** Settle the open question in favour of the in-run tidy before close-out. The readers read the PR head blind. The builder answers in its live session, where cost already attributes. The tidy and the notes update land in one PR. That removes the finished-session cost, the separate commit path for notes, and the second set of fixed costs. The trade is that the readers become a pre-merge step, and close-out needs a rule for claims that don't hold a merge. Then choose an area key the server can resolve for any repo, with areas.json as one input. A filed follow-on becomes the exception, for leftovers outside the change's area.

**The deeper issue.** The missing piece is a durable "this merged" producer that other steps can subscribe to. The Periodicals and the look-first change will want it too.

## Survey global: LIN-4347 @ eeda7e448

**Where it lands.** Three places that don't yet know about each other:

- **The merge seam.** `createPipelineMergeRecorder` (`lib/close-out-merges.js`) runs fire-and-forget beside the proxy's Done write (`routes/proxy-writes.js:539`), and the task-page check records merges through the same writer. **Nothing dispatches on a merge today.** The only precedent for Harbour starting a session itself is `lib/ci-wake-sweep.js`: a scheduler job that calls `enqueueFollowUp`, fails closed with no owner, and runs once per result by marker.
- **The stage registry.** `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` (1,258 lines) already has two post-merge readers: `retrospective-audit` (routed, files a follow-up per finding) and `retro` (hand-only). `close-out` already files outside follow-ups and fixes the citations its change made stale.
- **Docs.** `docs/` has 75 top-level files, many of them stale research notes. The Survey notebook is copied to main by hand, one ticket per copy (LIN-4314, LIN-4332).

It's getting better: four of the last ten merges were tidy-afters that merged copies into one owner.

**The obvious way.** New `blind-read` and `after-question` stages plus a merge hook would make a third post-merge reader beside `retrospective-audit` and `retro`, and a third filer of follow-ups. The registries would notice a new kind: the template-count test, `completion-signals`, stage traits, the prompt-size budget and `llm-jobs-census` all fail loudly. The notes have no such guard. A `docs/areas/*.md` that no prompt reads is one more file in `docs/`, and nothing would notice it going stale.

Two facts constrain the design:

1. **Notes on main mean every note write is a PR.** A read-only reader running after the merge can't write them. So either each reading spawns a notes PR, paying the fixed costs again, or the leftover read happens before the merge and the tidy and its notes entry ride in the same PR. That favours doing the tidy within the run, with review supplying the leftover read.
2. **Hooking the pipeline's Done write misses merges** that people make on GitHub. A sweep over merged events not yet read (the ci-wake-sweep shape) catches both seams.

"By area" already has a vocabulary in `scripts/code-shape/areas.json`, but a research tool owns it. Keying product notes on that file makes the product depend on research tooling. Keeping a separate list makes two area lists.

**Better, and within reach.**

- Narrow `retrospective-audit`, or add a leftover section to `review`, instead of adding a new stage beside them.
- Make the builder question a dispatch kind, so `readCost` shows its cost on the ticket.
- Give each state one home: a Linear follow-on will be done; an area note is known but unscheduled. Say so in close-out's text.
- Add a test that every notes file names a real area, and code that puts a ticket's area notes into its context, with a cap of their own, since prompt size is frozen.
- Seed the notes with the brief's leftovers.

**Better still, not this task's.** Move the area list into a registry the product owns. Merge `retro` and `retrospective-audit`. Split `docs/` into living docs and an archive.

## Size of the move (the person's call)

Err larger, John's standing answer. Since filing, John has asked for **the everyday version, not our research rig** (his note on this ticket). Both Surveys point the same way.

**Settle the open question in favour of the tidy inside the run.** Today, nothing in Harbour dispatches on a merge, the worker that merges can't start sessions, and a builder's session has usually stopped by the time anyone asks it something. So the leftover read happens before the merge. One reader looks at what the change left at its edges. John's own hint is that review, which already reads every change, may be the natural place for that read. The builder is asked what it left behind while its session is still live, at the end of its work, where its cost already shows on the ticket. The tidy, and its entry in the notes, ride in the same pull request as the change. That avoids a separate pull request for every notes write, and paying the fixed costs again for a follow-on ticket.

The blind readers judged from the code without the ticket because we were measuring. A leftover read that can see the ticket is fine for finding edges. Say what you chose and why. Folding the two existing after-merge readers (`retrospective-audit` and `retro`) into one would remove a step. If you think it should happen, raise it as a ruling rather than doing it.

**Good notes, kept with the code, by area.** This is the part that lasts. A note says what's been learned about making changes in that area, and what's waiting there, written so that the next builder in that area works differently for having read it. The notes need a home the product owns. The only area list today, `scripts/code-shape/areas.json`, is research tooling. The notes may cover simple-dispatcher as well as Harbour, so this ticket may touch both repositories. Each kind of leftover has one home: a follow-on ticket means it will be done, and a note means it's known but not scheduled. Don't make a third home beside the Survey notebook (`docs/plans/survey/`, kept on a research branch and copied to main by hand; see LIN-4316). Say what becomes of its knowledge about areas. Seed the notes with the entries already posted on this ticket.

A follow-on ticket becomes the exception, for leftovers outside the change's own area.

**Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself, and record why. Raise a ruling only for John's calls: how big a move is, what's spent, removing a step, and authority. Work that doesn't depend on a ruling keeps moving.

**Done when** a ticket's change merges with its own edges already tidied, or with a note saying what's waiting there, without anyone dispatching anything. The next ticket in that area is shown to have used that note, and the leftover step's cost shows on its ticket.

DECISION: Two sentences of the As-asked block aren't delivered in full by the plan. Do you accept both cuts? Building the plan doesn't wait on this, because neither answer changes what gets built.

1. "That follow-on goes through the look-first step like any ticket." This ticket files a follow-on as an ordinary ticket: As-asked block sealed, no plan, no size record. That makes it eligible for look-first. Running look-first automatically is LIN-4370's work, which is waiting on LIN-4369's replay. Until LIN-4370 lands, look-first on a follow-on is started by hand, like on any other ticket. **Recommendation: accept.** A second route built here would conflict with LIN-4370.

2. "A follow-on that both readers judge better gets none of its own." There are no readers any more (your 7 Nov ruling), so the condition can't be applied. What holds instead: every follow-on runs the same leftover step, and a leftover inside the area goes to the notes, never to a ticket. So a follow-on can only lead to another through a leftover outside its own area. **Recommendation: accept.** Follow-ons are already the exception, so such a chain stays rare.

Options for each: accept the cut / deliver it here (1: build a look-first route in this ticket; 2: give follow-ons a marker and never file a follow-on from one).

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Request Changes. Holding back the parent's wake is the guard this plan loosens, and the plan gives no way to release it when the queued `leftover` row ends without ever posting a result.

Blocking findings: 1

**How the plan meets what was asked.** It delivers "notes kept with the code on main, by area", "it answers LIN-4316" and "each of these steps shows its cost on the ticket" in full. Five narrowings each cite a comment from the person: one read that can see the ticket (7 Nov note); the read and the question happen before the merge (size comment); only "what did your change leave behind?" is asked (7 Nov note); a follow-on only for leftovers outside the area (size comment); and John's Done-when replaces "Done looks like" (size comment). The size comment counts as a ruling: `lib/size-of-move.js:16` treats `## Size of the move (the person's call)` comments as John's hand-written rulings. Two narrowings are not agreed yet ("That follow-on goes through the look-first step like any ticket"; "A follow-on that both readers judge better gets none of its own"). The open `DECISION:` asks about both. Either answer only adds work, so that question does not block the plan. Close-out must not count those two sentences as met until John answers.

**What I checked, and found true.** HEAD is still `eeda7e44` / `07c88f7`, so nothing has landed since the plan was written, and PR #2356 is still open.
- A finished cli/web session resumes. `RUN_STOPPED` covers only recorded stops (`lib/dispatch-factory.js:228-245`; SD `followup.js`, `docs/session-lifecycle.md` "Follow-ups").
- `/cost` already splits cost per dispatch, with `kind` and its own usage (`lib/cost-read.js:465-495`).
- A follow-up never counts toward the run limit or the duplicate guard, because both apply only to fresh rows (`dispatch-factory.js:342-348`).
- The leftover row's terminal will wake the parent. `_resolveEdgeDoc` walks `followUpTo` back to the edge, and `terminalWakeItems` is keyed on the row that posted, so a different beat still wakes it (`lib/dispatch-store.js`, the LIN-1357 block).
- Both `addFeedback` callers are where the plan cites them.
- Review's "Isolated, or One of a Class?" section exists (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js:911`).
- The anchor resolver still denylists `docs/plans/survey` (`tests/unit/docs-architecture-anchor-resolver.test.js:94`).

---

#### Blocking

**1. The held wake is released only by the leftover row's own terminal, and a queued row can end without one.** The plan's safeguards cover the cases where nothing gets queued: not eligible, owner refused, enqueue not 200, the hook throws. They don't cover a row that is queued but never runs:
- an unclaimed row expires after the queue TTL, 24 h (`dispatch-store.js:488`). The expiry sweep archives it as `expired` and posts no feedback (`:1679-1703`);
- a person cancels it from the queue, or Undo does (`removeItem` → `_archiveOrRestore(doc, 'cancelled')`, `:1571-1586`). Again no feedback;
- SD leaves it unclaimed when a follow-up without `force` finds a session that is still `ACTIVE` (`followup.js:105`, `shouldQueueIfBusy`). It then waits until it expires.

In each case the build's own wake was held back and nothing else wakes the parent. An autopilot ends up waiting forever, and nothing raises it. The liveness alarms are advisory, and they watch parked `[pending]` waits, not a parent waiting for a wake. That is the stranding the plan's own constraint forbids, just reached one step later.

*What must change:* the plan names what releases the held wake when a `leftover` row reaches `expired` or `cancelled` without a terminal, plus a witness that proves it. The smallest version: inject a hook into the store's archive path, the same way `provisionWakeCredential` is injected, so archiving a `leftover` row as `expired`/`cancelled` mints the build beat's held wake once. Add store-level witnesses: a queued leftover cancelled through `removeItem`, and one expired by the expiry sweep, each wake the parent exactly once with the build's outcome. If the plan picks a different release, such as a bounded sweep over held wakes, it needs the same two witnesses.

---

#### Notes for the builder (not blocking)

2. **A re-reported build `[done]` wakes the parent early.** The hook holds the first wake back, so the build's guard key never lands in `terminalWakeItems`. A retried `[done]` (LIN-3805 says retries can duplicate entries) then fails the "no `leftover` row yet" check. Under "every non-eligibility falls back", it wakes the parent while the leftover step is still running. Have the pure module return three outcomes: *queue*, *already queued for this producing row → hold back again*, and *not eligible → fall back*. Extend the plan's "re-report of the same `[done]`" witness to assert that the parent is not woken, and that the leftover's later `[done]` wakes it once.
3. **Decide eligibility from the lineage's base kind, not `doc.kind`.** A builder that parked on CI is resumed by `ci-wake-sweep` through `enqueueFollowUp`, which passes no kind, so the resumed row is `custom` (`deriveDispatchKind(undefined)`, `lib/prompt-templates.js:238`). SD points `itemId` at that row, so the terminal `[done]` lands on it. A `doc.kind === 'implementation'` check would miss every build that parked. Also exclude periodical Stage-2 runs, which are `kind: 'implementation'` rows carrying `periodicalId` (`lib/periodicals.js:1044`). Add witnesses: a build whose `[done]` lands on a ci-wake follow-up row queues a leftover; a periodical `implementation` row does not.
4. **`enqueueFollowUp` has no `kind` parameter** (`lib/follow-up-dispatch.js:194`), so add an optional pass-through. Recommendation: keep `leftover` a row-only kind like `wake` (`lib/run-view.js:125`; `tests/unit/task-page-loader.test.js:616` lists `wake` explicitly). Adding it to `DISPATCH_KINDS` would let any `/dispatch` caller create one, and a manual one would satisfy the once-per-ticket check.
5. **`force` must be true.** `followUpForLoop` takes a pipeline loop, not a raw row. The row being judged has just posted `[done]`, so it is terminal by definition. With `force: false`, a session not yet flipped from `ACTIVE` gets `session-busy` (feeds finding 1).
6. **The owner gate needs inputs at both entrances.** `proxy-runner.js` has `req.proxyWorkspaceId` (`routes/proxy.js:610`) and `publicOrigin(req)`. The dispatch-token feedback route in `routes/dispatch.js` has no workspace id, so it needs a resolver (`createTickWorkspaceResolver` in `lib/ci-wake-sweep.js` is the model) or it will always fall back. Log every fallback with a reason that is easy to find (for example `[leftover] skipped reason=…`), so a hook that always falls back can be seen. The post-deploy demonstration is the witness that the real wiring works.
7. **Workspace halt.** `guardRunStopped` doesn't look at the workspace halt. Make an active halt a non-eligibility (fall back to the plain wake), so Harbour doesn't start new sessions under a halt.
8. **The parent now gets the leftover's feedback instead of the build's.** `buildWakeFollowUp(edgeDoc, updated)` carries the producing row's entries. Have the leftover prompt require the terminal comment to restate the PR URL and head SHA, so the autopilot still sees what the build's wake would have told it.
9. **`GROUNDING_BY_KIND`.** `WORK` is one shared array for `plan`, `bug`, `research`, `design`, `spike`, `review` and also `scoping`, `plan-review`, `close-out`, `breakdown`, `blocked` (`lib/prompt-formatters.js:612-613`). Adding the pointer to `WORK` would change scoping's bytes, so split the array. `implementation` uses `GROUNDING_NOTES`, which is also the fallback for unknown kinds (`:638`), so a note added there reaches those as well.
10. **The registry covers code paths only.** Under first-match order, `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md`, `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md` and `tests/` match no area, and `lib/as-asked.js` falls through to the `^lib/` catch-all in "Other features". For the two seeds whose first path is a doc or a script, cite the code owner first (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js`). Don't add `docs/`/`scripts/` patterns, which would change the code-shape census and cochange counts (the LIN-3829 caution in `tests/unit/area-map-placement.test.js`). Place `as-asked.js` on purpose, with a placement assertion. The plan's second demonstration expects LIN-4349/4350 in "LLM & prompts".
11. **Optional:** give agents a one-line resolver (e.g. `node scripts/areas-of.mjs <paths>`) and name it in the grounding pointer. First-match regex order is easy to get wrong by eye (see `as-asked.js` above).
12. `docs/areas/` is not denylisted, so the docs anchor sweep will check notes. Cite files, not line numbers.

**Plan revised (revision 2), answering the 8 Nov Plan Review Verdict.** The description holds the one current plan.

- **Blocking 1 (fixed):** the held wake has a durable hold. The `leftover` row carries `heldWakeFor`, declared in `lib/dispatch-fields.js` so it survives the archive hop. It is released by whichever comes first:
  - the row's own terminal;
  - `_archiveItem` archiving the row `cancelled` or `expired`. That covers `removeItem`, Undo, the stopped-run cleanup and the `cleanup()` expiry sweep.

  The release mints under the build's guard key through `_mintWake`'s CAS, so it fires exactly once. It keeps the stopped-parent gate. It takes credentials from a late-bound provisioner factory, wired in `server.js` like `setHaltReader`. New witnesses: a cancel and an expiry each wake the parent exactly once with the build's outcome, and a re-report after a release adds nothing.
- **2 (fixed):** the pure decision returns queue / hold / not eligible. A re-reported `[done]` holds again, or re-runs the idempotent release if the row was cancelled or expired.
- **3 (fixed):** eligibility comes from the lineage root. Periodical and lane rows are excluded, and a build whose `[done]` lands on a ci-wake row is witnessed.
- **4, 5 (fixed):** `kind` is passed through `enqueueFollowUp`. `leftover` is a row-only kind, kept out of `DISPATCH_KINDS`. `force: true`.
- **6 (fixed):** the hook is built once in `server.js` with a workspace resolver and `resolveEmailLinkOrigin()`, and handed to both entrances. A route-level witness at each entrance, plus a `[leftover] skipped reason=` log line.
- **7 (fixed):** an active halt, `pause` or `stop`, means not eligible.
- **8 (fixed):** the leftover's terminal comment restates the PR URL and head SHA.
- **9 (fixed):** the seven kinds get their own grounding list. `WORK`, `GROUNDING_NOTES` and the fallback stay byte-identical, and so do the scoping, Survey, close-out and unknown-kind prompts.
- **10 (fixed):** the registry stays code-only. Seeds about a doc or a script cite their code owner first, and `lib/as-asked.js` is placed deliberately with an assertion. This replaces "fix the registry".
